articles.title: Fracture orthopedic risk of non-home discharge score II (FORD-II).
articles.authors: Salman SG, Phadke R, Carlin T, Ramirez J, Mendez-Reyes JE, Hoffman MK, et al.
articles.population: Adults with fracture diagnoses from a national trauma registry
articles.outcomes: Non-home discharge to inpatient rehabilitation, skilled nursing facility, long-term acute care or intermediate care
articles.take_home: FORD-II is a scoring tool completed at hospital admission that can identify fracture patients likely to need ongoing care in a facility rather than going home, with higher accuracy than previous tools. Using this score to trigger early planning could help hospitals arrange appropriate care faster and potentially reduce costs.

articles.title: Survival and quality of life after treatment of geriatric odontoid fractures.
articles.authors: Oberthur S, Singer AK, Roch PJ, Weiser L, Lehmann W, Sehmisch S
articles.population: Geriatric patients (mean age 78.9 years) with odontoid fractures
articles.sample_size: 93 patients (59% surgical, 41% conservative); 40 respondents for quality of life assessment
articles.outcomes: 1-year mortality, pain (Visual Analog Scale), neck disability (Neck Disability Index), quality of life (Short Form-36)
articles.take_home: Older patients with odontoid fractures had a 1-year death rate of 27% and better survival with surgery, but those treated without surgery reported lower pain and better overall quality of life. Treatment should be individualised based on how ill the patient is overall.

articles.title: External Iliac artery injury in severe pelvic ring trauma: Limb salvage or early hemipelvectomy? A case series.
articles.authors: Yang YJ, Lai CY, Tsai PJ, Chen IJ, Liu CH, Yu YH
articles.population: Patients with combined external iliac artery injury and pelvic ring injury from high-energy trauma
articles.outcomes: Limb salvage success rate, need for hemipelvectomy, patient survival, infection and necrosis complications
articles.take_home: Attempts to save the limb failed in all 5 patients despite trying to restore blood flow in 2 cases, with 4 eventually needing removal of the hip and leg (hemipelvectomy) due to tissue death and infection. The study suggests that when there is severe tissue damage alongside this type of injury, early amputation may be better than prolonged attempts at salvage.

articles.title: The biomechanical performance of the both-column screw in posterior acetabular column fractures.
articles.authors: Ozturk V, Hurmeydan OM, Celik T, Bayrak A, Kural C, Bilgili MG
articles.population: Acetabular posterior column fractures
articles.outcomes: Stress on screw and bone, deformation, fracture gap, and sliding distance across five fixation methods under three loading conditions
articles.take_home: Double both-column screws provided the best stability for posterior acetabular column fractures, with less deformation and fracture displacement than single screws or plate-based methods. This suggests double screws could be a good alternative to traditional plate fixation for these fractures.

articles.title: Balanced cable bone transport of the tibia using automated motorized struts.
articles.authors: Wellings EP, Blair JA
articles.population: Patients undergoing tibial bone transport with average defect size of 102 mm
articles.outcomes: Union rate, complications, external fixation index, bone healing index, and mechanical alignment
articles.take_home: Automated struts can successfully power bone transport in the tibia, but complications occurred in most patients including strut malfunctions in 4 cases and pin tract infections in 4 cases. The approach is feasible and may help patients comply with treatment, though further refinement is needed.

articles.title: Traumatic Posterior Dislocation Is Associated with Posterior Acromial Morphology.
articles.authors: Werthel JD, Vervaecke A, Petit M, Jamei-Martel O, Gerber C
articles.population: Patients with first-time acute traumatic shoulder dislocation
articles.outcomes: Posterior acromial tilt, posterior acromial coverage, posterior acromial height, and critical shoulder angle measured on radiographs
articles.take_home: People who had a traumatic posterior shoulder dislocation had different shoulder blade shapes compared to those with anterior dislocations, particularly a higher and more tilted back part of the shoulder blade. These shape differences may make posterior dislocations more likely to happen.

articles.title: De-Implementation of Routine Radiographs in the Follow-up of Wrist and Ankle Fractures in Dutch Hospitals.
articles.authors: Vuijk DA, Krijnen P, Eggebeen NJ, Schipper IB, van Bodegom-Vos L, Termaat MF
articles.population: Adults with distal radial fractures or malleolar fractures treated at 5 hospitals in the West Netherlands
articles.sample_size: 1497 patients (846 historical controls, 337 after dissemination, 314 after de-implementation)
articles.outcomes: Number of routine follow-up radiographs per patient; proportion of patients without routine follow-up imaging; total number of radiographs
articles.take_home: Hospitals significantly reduced unnecessary follow-up X-rays for wrist and ankle fractures by sharing research evidence and using tailored education strategies. This approach was safe and reduced low-value imaging without compromising care.

articles.title: Incidence of nonunion after open tibia fractures in Malawi : associated factors and Radiographic Union Score for Tibial fractures reliability.
articles.authors: Schade AT, Dimock R, Mendes da Costa T, Nohakhelha N, Mwafulirwa K, Mkochi V, et al.
articles.population: Adults with open tibia fractures in Malawi
articles.sample_size: 287 participants enrolled; 177 with follow-up data at one year
articles.outcomes: Nonunion rates at one year (25.4% overall; 34.2% with fracture-related infection); reliability of RUST score (moderate interobserver agreement); functional outcomes using SMFA score
articles.take_home: About one in four patients with open tibia fractures in Malawi had nonunion at one year, with infection significantly increasing this risk. The RUST scoring system is moderately reliable for assessing bone healing and correlates with how well patients function, even when X-ray quality is variable.

articles.title: Subtrochanteric varisation explains age-related changes in proximal femoral morphology and has implications for hip arthroplasty and trauma surgery.
articles.authors: Ecker N, Simon M, Lisitano L, Fenwick A, Betsch M, Donhauser M, et al.
articles.population: Patients of different ages undergoing pelvic-leg CT angiography
articles.outcomes: Correlation between caput-collum-diaphyseal angle and trochanteric rotation/offset parameters; associations with age, bone quality, and femoral morphology
articles.take_home: The study found that older people's hip bones develop a bent inward (varus) shape mainly in the area below the trochanter, which has important implications for hip replacement and fracture surgery planning. This age-related change is linked to weaker bone quality and affects how surgeons should position implants.

articles.title: Today's perspectives and challenges in moving management of patients with open tibial fractures forward in the Netherlands.
articles.authors: Dibbits MHJ, Rakhorst HA, Stirler V, de Groot R, van Egmond PW, Krijgh DD, et al.
articles.population: Plastic and orthopaedic trauma surgeons across Dutch trauma centres
articles.sample_size: 42 surgeons from all 11 level 1 centres and 13 specialists from level 2 centres
articles.outcomes: Case volume, timing of soft tissue coverage for open tibial fractures, barriers to achieving coverage within 72 hours
articles.take_home: Soft tissue coverage for open tibial fractures is achieved within 72 hours in only 6% of Dutch cases, mainly due to limited operating theatre availability and prioritization issues. Most centres manage 10-20 open tibial fractures annually but struggle with the guideline recommendation to cover wounds within a week.

articles.title: AI-assisted holosight robotic percutaneous minimally invasive surgery for pelvic fractures: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Zhu L, Wang H, Qi X, Zhang T, Wang L, Jiao Y, et al.
articles.population: Patients with pelvic fractures
articles.outcomes: Operative time, intraoperative blood loss, fluoroscopy frequency, guidewire insertion attempts, Majeed functional scores, fracture healing time
articles.take_home: Robot-assisted surgery with AI planning for pelvic fractures resulted in shorter surgery time, less blood loss, fewer X-rays and fewer needle attempts compared to standard fluoroscopy-guided surgery. Both approaches achieved similar functional results for patients.

articles.title: Prehospital pelvic binder use and transfusion requirements in patients with pelvic fractures: A nationwide propensity-matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Matsumoto S, Aoki M, Shimizu M
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Adult patients with blunt pelvic fractures
articles.sample_size: 10,332 eligible patients; 182 with prehospital pelvic binder and 546 matched controls analysed
articles.outcomes: Primary: 24-hour red blood cell transfusion volume. Secondary: in-hospital mortality and pelvic angioembolization rates
articles.take_home: Prehospital pelvic binders did not reduce the amount of blood transfused or save lives in patients with pelvic fractures, but were associated with more patients needing angioembolization (a procedure to stop bleeding). This suggests binders may change how doctors treat bleeding rather than preventing it.

articles.title: The application of allgower-donati suture in obese patients with closed Schatzker type V and VI tibial plateau fractures.
articles.authors: Feng J, Hou J, Wang Y, Lu H, Wang X
articles.population: Patients with closed Schatzker type V and VI tibial plateau fractures, stratified by body mass index
articles.outcomes: Modified ASEPSIS score (postoperative days 1-7 and 7-14), VAS pain scores (days 3, 7, 14), SF-36 physical health scores at 12 weeks, wound complications
articles.take_home: Obese patients had more short-term wound complications after this fracture surgery than normal-weight patients. The Allgower-Donati suture technique showed promise in reducing these complications in obese patients, though larger studies are needed to confirm this finding.

articles.title: Posterior-only versus combined anterior-posterior stabilization in fragility fractures of the pelvis: Reoperations, perioperative burden, and radiographic outcomes.
articles.authors: Gewiess J, Karampitianis S, Bastian JD, Lustenberger T, Deml MC, Tinner C
articles.population: Adults aged 65 years or older with fragility fractures of the pelvis involving both anterior and posterior pelvic rings, treated surgically between 2013 and 2024
articles.sample_size: 55 patients (31 combined anterior-posterior stabilization, 24 posterior-only stabilization)
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: reoperation within 2 years. Secondary outcomes: blood loss, operative time, length of hospital stay, and radiographic outcomes including fracture gap, pelvic symmetry, and vertical alignment
articles.take_home: Posterior-only surgical fixation for fragility fractures involving both pelvic rings resulted in less bleeding and shorter surgery time than combined anterior-posterior fixation, without increasing the need for repeat surgery or causing differences in how the fractures healed on imaging. The study suggests that adding anterior fixation may not be routinely necessary for these fractures in older adults.

articles.title: Regional versus general anesthesia in volar plate fixation of distal radius fractures: An AO/OTA-stratified matched-pair analysis of radiographic reduction quality.
articles.authors: Pieringer A, Hinkelmann MA, Zumsteg J, Pape HC, Allemann F, Barthel C
articles.population: Patients with operatively treated distal radius fractures
articles.outcomes: Radiographic reduction quality (primary), operative time, complications, wrist movement, and Soong grade (secondary)
articles.take_home: For complex fractures, general anaesthesia produced better alignment on X-rays than regional anaesthesia, with fewer patients developing a tilted wrist position. However, early clinical outcomes and movement were similar between the two approaches.

articles.title: Comparing the epidemiology and associations of single- versus multi-level traumatic spinal fractures at a tertiary referral hospital in Ethiopia.
articles.authors: Mengistu MG, Yazdanpanah S, Damenu H, Baz S, Hanks HE, Dai J, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using prospectively maintained registry
articles.population: Patients with traumatic spinal fractures presenting to a tertiary referral hospital in Ethiopia
articles.outcomes: Demographics, cause of injury, neurological injury severity (ASIA grade), 30-day mortality, hospital length of stay
articles.take_home: Patients with fractures at multiple levels of the spine had more severe nerve damage and a higher death rate (27.5% versus 8.2%) compared to those with fractures at a single level, and they stayed in hospital longer. These findings suggest that multi-level spinal fractures are more serious injuries that require better treatment strategies in low- and middle-income countries.

articles.title: The influence of pelvic tilt on regional bone mineral density of the sacrum: A quantitative CT analysis.
articles.authors: Klockner FS, von Stosch D, Jackle K, Malik HA, Roch J, Meier MP, et al.
articles.population: Adults who underwent spine CT imaging and lumbar spine radiographs
articles.outcomes: Association between pelvic tilt and trabecular bone mineral density in the sacrum measured at five regions within S1 vertebra
articles.take_home: Increased pelvic tilt was associated with lower bone mineral density in the sacrum, particularly in the sacral wings and main vertebral body, independent of age and sex. This suggests that how the pelvis sits affects bone strength in the sacrum.

articles.title: Trends in medical healthcare complaints at two Danish orthopedic departments - A descriptive study.
articles.authors: Lyndrup O, Christiansen JL, Lorentsen CJ, Simony A
articles.population: Formal complaints regarding medical treatment at two orthopaedic departments at Lillebaelt Hospital, Denmark
articles.outcomes: Number of complaints by staff group, setting (elective or acute), reason for complaint, and distribution between hospitals
articles.take_home: Most complaints involved consultants rather than junior doctors, and most were about treatment rather than behaviour or examination. Younger doctors should have less concern about receiving complaints as few involved them directly.

articles.title: What is the relative importance of anterior ring intramedullary implant diameter and cortical purchase on outcomes following percutaneous fixation of lateral compression pelvic ring injuries?
articles.authors: Hoskins W, Parola R, Gusho C, Bravin D, Crist B, Wenzel A, et al.
articles.population: Patients with acute lateral compression pelvic ring injuries treated with percutaneous anterior and posterior fixation
articles.sample_size: 181 lateral compression injuries (127 LC1, 29 LC2, 25 LC3); mean age 59.2 years, 52% female
articles.outcomes: Primary: unplanned reoperation for loss of fixation, deformity, nonunion or symptomatic implant (2.8% overall). Secondary: radiographic loss of reduction (9.4% experienced deformity)
articles.take_home: Bicortical implants (going through both sides of bone) significantly reduced deformity rates compared with unicortical implants, but implant diameter size made no difference when bicortical fixation was used. Larger implants offered no additional benefit over medium-sized implants.

articles.title: Fall height is inversely associated with mortality in geriatric trauma patients undergoing trauma team activation and whole-body CT: A retrospective cohort analysis.
articles.authors: Erdle B, Pietsch C, Holzfurtner L, Siegel M, Muhlenfeld M, Frodl A, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 65 years and over who fell and underwent trauma team activation and whole-body CT scanning
articles.outcomes: In-hospital mortality, injury patterns, injury severity score (ISS), geriatric trauma outcome score (GTOS)
articles.take_home: Older adults who fell from ground level had higher death rates than those who fell from greater heights, even though their overall injury severity scores were similar. This suggests that ground-level falls in elderly people should not be underestimated as they can cause serious injuries, particularly to the head and neck.

articles.title: Injury mechanism patterns, mortality predictors, and resource utilization in pediatric trauma in Karachi, Pakistan: A seven-year registry study.
articles.authors: Lahoti GA, Ismail H, Kewalramani D, Dalal N, Benton J, Choron RL, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively maintained trauma registry
articles.population: Children and adolescents with traumatic injuries in Karachi, Pakistan
articles.outcomes: In-hospital mortality, injury mechanisms, resource utilisation (blood transfusion, operative intervention, ICU admission, intubation)
articles.take_home: Motorcycle crashes and falls are the leading causes of serious injury in children in Karachi, with overall mortality of 15.1% but much higher in infants (34.9%). The study found that actual death rates exceeded predictions, particularly in younger children, suggesting that improvements in trauma care systems and prehospital transport are needed.

articles.title: Residual instability of the radiocapitellar joint after treatment of acute pediatric Monteggia fractures: A single-center experience.
articles.authors: Polat M, Akgun H, Cat G, Aydin A
articles.population: Children with acute Monteggia fracture-dislocations
articles.outcomes: Radiocapitellar joint instability, ulnar angulation, radial head displacement, elbow function (Mayo Elbow Performance Score), treatment success rates
articles.take_home: Surgery was successful in all patients, but conservative treatment only worked in 68% of cases. Greater initial bending of the forearm bone and certain fracture patterns were linked to treatment failure and ongoing joint instability.

articles.title: Treatment-center variations in open versus closed reduction for nonelderly femoral neck fractures.
articles.authors: Wahle CF, Anoushiravani AA, Kakulamarri S, Patterson JT, Collinge CA, Morshed S
articles.population: Skeletally mature patients aged 18-60 years with operative repair of femoral neck fractures at 25 North American Level 1 Trauma Centers
articles.outcomes: Variation in use of open versus closed reduction for femoral neck fractures across treatment centers, accounting for patient and fracture characteristics
articles.take_home: Different trauma centres used open reduction surgery at significantly different rates for femoral neck fractures, even when accounting for patient characteristics and injury severity, suggesting treatment decisions may be influenced by factors beyond medical necessity.

articles.title: Post-operative weight-bearing practices following lower limb fracture surgery: A National multidisciplinary survey of concordance with AO foundation guidelines.
articles.authors: Tsohar TN, Khoury A, Barzel O, Dudkiewicz I
articles.population: Israeli orthopaedic specialists, trauma specialists, residents, and rehabilitation team members
articles.sample_size: 79 clinicians (44 orthopaedic specialists, 16 trauma specialists, 13 residents, 6 rehabilitation team)
articles.outcomes: Adherence to AO Foundation guidelines for weight-bearing prescriptions after lower limb fracture surgery, measured across four standardised clinical scenarios
articles.take_home: Only one in ten clinicians followed AO guidelines consistently across all fracture types, with compliance varying widely by fracture complexity and clinician speciality. The study suggests moving to newer qualitative frameworks for weight-bearing instructions could reduce dangerous inconsistencies in how clinicians interpret guidance.

articles.title: Pediatric firework-related upper extremity injuries: A 10-year review of cases presented to United States emergency departments, 2015-2024.
articles.authors: Zediker CR, Crowl KE, Krul JS, Megafu M, Li X, Parisien RL, et al.
articles.population: Children and teenagers with firework-related upper extremity injuries treated in US emergency departments
articles.outcomes: Injury rates, demographic patterns, anatomical injury locations, and types of injury; treatment outcomes including discharge or hospitalisation rates
articles.take_home: Between 2015 and 2024, firework injuries to children's upper limbs were most common in teenage boys aged 12-17 years, with burns to the hands and fingers being the main injury type. Most children were treated and sent home, but some required hospital admission.

articles.title: Outcomes of conservative management of CT-diagnosed hemothorax in chest trauma: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Alomar Z, El-Khatib A, Khreibeh M, Refai A, Alomari M, Alomar A, et al.
articles.population: Stable patients with chest trauma and small-volume hemothorax diagnosed on CT scan
articles.sample_size: 1679 patients managed conservatively (from 3030 total patients across 10 studies)
articles.outcomes: Success rate of conservative management (81%), need for delayed chest tube drainage (19%), need for surgery (1.8%), and causes of treatment failure
articles.take_home: Small bleeds in the chest cavity (less than 300 cc) from trauma can usually be managed safely by watching and monitoring rather than inserting a drain immediately, though about 1 in 5 patients will eventually need a drain inserted later. The study supports trying conservative management in stable patients, but more high-quality research is needed before this becomes standard practice.
